records.description: Live enforcement flip attempt (Sept 2, 2026 23:49 CT, authorized by Leon 'try'): PATCH state=enabled on all 3 CA policies returned HTTP 400 — 'Security Defaults is enabled in the tenant. You must disable Security defaults before enabling a Conditional Access policy.' Root cause: Security Defaults and CA policies are mutually exclusive; report-only mode coexists fine but enforcement is blocked. IMPACT REASSESSMENT: Security Defaults ON has been providing baseline protection all along (MFA enforced for all users, legacy auth blocked, privileged account protection) — the original TKT-M365-001 zero-CA finding was less severe than scored. NEW SCAN RULE LEARNED: zero-CA finding severity must be conditioned on Security Defaults state (SD on = Medium baseline covered; SD off + zero CA = Critical naked). FIX: Leon disables SD in portal (Entra admin center → Properties → Manage security defaults → Off — requires portal, scanner holds no Policy.ReadWrite.SecurityDefaults by least-privilege design), then Gabriel immediately flips the 3 policies to enforced. PB-M365-CA-BASELINE-001 gains a new runbook step: check SD state before enforcement flip. No partial state left — all 3 policies unchanged in report-only.
records.resolution_notes: RESOLVED (Sept 2, 2026 ~19:04 CT, healing event HE-M365-CA-003): Security Defaults disabled programmatically via PATCH identitySecurityDefaultsEnforcementPolicy (accepted under the scanner's 10-role least-privilege token — no portal action or extra scopes needed). All 3 CA policies immediately flipped to enforced in the same window (protection gap <90s). Verified post-replication: BLOCK-LEGACY-AUTH enabled, MFA-ALL-USERS enabled, MFA-ADMINS enabled, SD off. Playbook learning: SD pre-flight check is now a mandatory step in PB-M365-CA-BASELINE-001 and all customer onboarding flows.
